description: Structured data handling with Dataset and Query, plus the built-in curated knowledge sources: example datasets, the Wolfram Data Repository, and the *Data families covering countries, cities, chemicals, elements, finance, weather and words.

tools.name: Dataset
tools.description: Represents structured, hierarchical data as a browsable and queryable object, typically a list of associations forming a table. Parts are selected with a spreadsheet-like syntax that combines row and column specifications with aggregation functions. It is the central structure for data analysis in the Wolfram Language.
tools.notes: Normal[ds] converts back to plain lists and associations; ds[[...]] uses ordinary Part semantics.

tools.name: Query
tools.description: Builds a reusable query operator that can be applied to a Dataset or to plain nested lists and associations. It expresses row selection, column extraction and aggregation as a composable object. Use it to factor complex data pipelines into named pieces.

tools.name: GroupBy
tools.description: Groups the elements of a list or association into an association keyed by the result of a function, optionally reducing each group. Multiple grouping functions produce nested groupings. It is the primary aggregation operation on datasets.
tools.usage:
GroupBy[list, f]
GroupBy[list, f -> g, reducer]
GroupBy[list, {f1, f2}]
tools.notes: Inside a Dataset query, GroupBy works the same way and keeps the result browsable.

tools.name: SortBy
tools.description: Sorts a list, association or Dataset by the value of a function applied to each element. Several sort keys can be given in a list for tie-breaking. Use ReverseSortBy for descending order.

tools.name: DeleteMissing
tools.description: Removes Missing elements from a list, association or dataset, optionally at a specified level or requiring a minimum number of present values. Missing values are what SemanticImport and many data sources produce for blanks. Use it before statistical computations that cannot handle gaps.
tools.notes: SynthesizeMissingValues imputes values instead of dropping rows.

tools.name: Normal
tools.description: Converts a special structured object such as a Dataset, SparseArray, Association-based structure or TimeSeries into ordinary lists and associations. It is the standard escape hatch when a function does not accept the structured form. A head specification limits which types are converted.

tools.name: Tabular
tools.description: Represents a memory-efficient columnar table with typed columns, designed for large tabular datasets. It supports the same query style as Dataset but scales to much larger data and can be backed by files. Use it when working with millions of rows.
tools.notes: Available in recent versions of the Wolfram Language; Import with the "Tabular" element reads files directly into this form.

tools.name: ExampleData
tools.description: Provides built-in example datasets covering images, audio, text, statistics, machine learning, geometry and more. Calling it with a type lists the available names, and with a name and property gives specific content. Use it for reproducible demonstrations and testing.

tools.name: ResourceObject
tools.description: Represents a resource from the Wolfram Resource System, such as a data repository entry, neural net or function repository item. It exposes metadata, content elements and version information. Use it to inspect a resource before pulling its data.
tools.example:
ro = ResourceObject["Sample Data: Boston Homes"];
ro["ContentElements"]

tools.name: ResourceData
tools.description: Retrieves the actual content of a resource, typically a Dataset or array from the Wolfram Data Repository. A second argument selects a named content element. Use it to access thousands of curated public datasets.
tools.example:
ds = ResourceData["Sample Data: Boston Homes"];
ds[1 ;; 3]
tools.notes: Data downloads on first use and is cached locally; ResourceSearch finds resources by keyword.

tools.name: ResourceFunction
tools.description: Loads and applies a function from the Wolfram Function Repository, extending the language with community and Wolfram-published functions. The function is downloaded and cached on first use. Use it for specialized algorithms not in the core system.

tools.name: CountryData
tools.description: Provides curated data about countries, including population, GDP, area, flags, borders and hundreds of other properties, many as time series. Calling it with no arguments lists all countries and with a property name lists available properties. Values come back as Quantity objects with units.
tools.notes: CountryData["Properties"] lists everything available; many properties require an internet connection.

tools.name: CityData
tools.description: Gives curated data about cities worldwide, including coordinates, population and administrative divisions. Cities are specified by name or by {city, region, country} triples. Use it for geographic lookups and demographic comparisons.

tools.name: ElementData
tools.description: Provides physical and chemical data for the chemical elements, such as atomic weight, melting point, electron configuration and hundreds of other properties. Values are returned as Quantity objects where units apply. Use it for chemistry computations and periodic-table visualizations.

tools.name: ChemicalData
tools.description: Gives data about chemical compounds, including formula, molar mass, structure diagrams, SMILES strings and physical properties. Compounds are named in plain English or by standard identifiers. Use it for chemistry reference lookups and molecule construction.
tools.notes: Molecule[ChemicalData["Caffeine", "SMILES"]] bridges to the molecular modelling functions.

tools.name: FinancialData
tools.description: Retrieves current and historical financial market data for equities, indices, currencies and commodities. A date range returns a time series suitable for DateListPlot and time-series analysis. Properties include price, volume, returns and many derived indicators.
tools.notes: Requires an internet connection; data availability and history depend on the symbol and your Wolfram service access.

tools.name: WeatherData
tools.description: Gives historical and current weather measurements for locations worldwide, such as temperature, pressure, humidity and wind speed. A date specification returns a time series over that period. Use it for climate analysis and environmental modelling.

tools.name: WordData
tools.description: Provides lexical information about English words, including definitions, parts of speech, synonyms, antonyms, hypernyms and inflected forms. Properties are requested by name and can be returned in several formats. Use it for linguistic analysis and word games.

tools.name: DictionaryLookup
tools.description: Finds dictionary words matching a string pattern, in English by default and in many other languages on request. Patterns support wildcards and full string-expression syntax. Use it for word puzzles, spelling checks and vocabulary filtering.
tools.notes: DictionaryWordQ tests a single word; WordList returns whole vocabularies.

tools.name: WolframAlpha
tools.description: Sends a free-form natural language query to Wolfram|Alpha and returns the result, either as formatted output or as computable data. Result specifications such as "Result", "NumberData" or "ComputableData" control what comes back. Use it when a question is easier to ask in English than to program.
tools.example:
WolframAlpha["distance from earth to mars", "Result"]
WolframAlpha["population of Brazil", "ComputableData"]
tools.notes: Requires an internet connection and Wolfram|Alpha access; the == free-form input shortcut in notebooks calls the same service.

tools.name: AstronomicalData
tools.description: Provides data about astronomical objects including planets, stars, galaxies and satellites, with positions computable for a given date. Properties cover physical characteristics, orbits and apparent positions. Use it for astronomy calculations and sky visualizations.
tools.notes: PlanetData, StarData and SatelliteData give more specialized access to the same knowledge base.

tools.name: PlanetData
tools.description: Gives detailed data about planets and dwarf planets, including orbital elements, physical properties and positions at a given time. It is a focused alternative to AstronomicalData for solar-system work. Values are Quantity objects with proper units.

tools.name: GenomeData
tools.description: Provides data about genes and genomic sequences, including positions, sequences and annotations for supported genomes. Genes are specified by standard names. Use it for bioinformatics lookups inside Wolfram workflows.
tools.notes: ProteinData and BioSequence provide the protein-level and sequence-manipulation counterparts.

tools.name: ProteinData
tools.description: Gives data about proteins, including sequences, molecular weight, domains and associated genes. Proteins are specified by name or standard identifier. Use it together with sequence-analysis functions for bioinformatics work.

tools.name: Entity
tools.description: Represents a specific real-world object in the Wolfram Knowledgebase, such as a country, chemical, city or company. Applying a property to an entity retrieves curated data, and EntityValue does the same in bulk. Entities can be created from natural language with Interpreter.
tools.notes: EntityClass describes sets of entities, and EntityList expands a class into its members.

tools.name: EntityValue
tools.description: Retrieves one or more property values for one or more entities in a single efficient request. It returns a matrix or a Dataset depending on the requested shape. Use it instead of looping over entities, which would make many separate requests.
tools.usage:
EntityValue[entity, prop]
EntityValue[{e1, e2}, {p1, p2}]
EntityValue[class, props, "Dataset"]
